meta.title: Export Chrome Bookmarks to CSV | Snug
meta.description: Export Chrome bookmarks to CSV with Snug: one row per bookmark, columns title, url and folder, and how a spreadsheet reads them. Checked {date}.

title: How do I export my Chrome bookmarks to CSV?
directAnswer: Chrome's help describes one export format, {fromExportFormats}, reached through {fromExportPath}. For CSV, use Snug's Export page: it writes one row per bookmark with title, url and folder columns, for only the folders you pick. Menu paths checked {date}.

builtIn.title: The built-in method
builtIn.intro: Chrome's help describes one export format, {fromExportFormats}, so the browser has no CSV or JSON option of its own. Its export is still the right choice when the file goes to another browser.
steps: Save the file. Chrome names it {fromExportFile} by default.
For rows in a spreadsheet, continue with Snug below.

carriesOver.title: What the CSV contains
carriesOver.intro: The first row names the columns. Each bookmark then gets one row, and folders get no row of their own.
items: Columns: title, url and folder. Date added, Date last used and Include favicons add dateAdded, dateLastUsed and iconData after them.
Folders: the folder column holds the full path, joined by /, starting with the top folder such as Bookmarks bar. Hide parent folder keeps only that top folder.
Quoting: every field is in double quotes, and a quote inside a field is doubled. A / or \ in a folder name gets a backslash, so Q3/Q4 appears as Q3\/Q4.
Spreadsheets: a field that starts with =, +, - or @ gets a leading apostrophe, so a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula.
Dates: dateAdded and dateLastUsed are whole seconds since 1970, not milliseconds.

withSnug.title: Export CSV with Snug
withSnug.intro: Snug runs in Chrome and other Chromium browsers. Its Export page lets you choose what goes into the file and how it is named.
steps: Install Snug from the Chrome Web Store.
Open Snug's Export page. Search for bookmarks, then tick single bookmarks or whole folders, or use Select all bookmarks.
Open Export options to add Date added, Date last used or Include favicons as extra columns, or to turn on Hide parent folder.
Edit Filename template to name the file. For example, %yyyy%mm%dd myPc gives a name such as 20260930 myPc.csv.
Click Export N bookmarks, where N is the count of what you ticked. Snug downloads the file.
withSnug.snapshot: The popup exports the whole tree in one click. Without a template, Snug names the file Bookmarks_<date>_<time>, for example Bookmarks_2026-10-03_14-05-09.

sample.title: A real sample
sample.intro: This is the exporter's own output for a small test tree: folders named Dev, "Tools" and Q3/Q4 on the Bookmarks bar, and one bookmark in Other bookmarks.

goesWrong.title: If something goes wrong
items: Commas or quotes split a title across cells. Snug quotes every field, so import the file as CSV with the double quote as the text qualifier and Comma, and "quotes" stays in one cell.
The folder column shows a backslash. A / inside a folder name is written \/ so that / stays the path separator.
A cell begins with an apostrophe. Snug adds it to values starting with =, +, - or @ so they are not run as formulas.
Only some folders should be in the file. The popup exports the whole tree. Use the Export page and tick the folders you want.
You need the rows back in a browser. Snug's Import page reads CSV and uses the folder column to rebuild folders. For another browser's import, use the HTML file from Chrome's built-in export.

verified: The menu path and export format were read from the official help pages of {fromName} on {date}. Menus change between versions, so check the source if a path differs on your screen. Column names and escaping come from Snug's CSV exporter and its tests.
